title: Deleting witness literals does not project an inconsistent equality or order pattern.
details:
[Zapletal, *Undergraduate logic sequence: the notes*](https://people.clas.ufl.edu/zapletal/files/notesset3.pdf),
2014-11-21, §6.3, proofs of Theorems 6.3.2 and 6.3.4, pp. 75–77
(PDF pages 79–81). Type: invalid elimination step.

The stated complete-conjunction convention does not require consistency. The
proof claims that existential projection is obtained by erasing all literals
mentioning the witness. Complete an equality pattern containing
`x₀=x₁`, `x₁=y`, and `x₀≠y` by supplying all remaining pair decisions. The whole
pattern has no realization, although its retained `x₀=x₁` pattern is consistent.
Thus erasing the witness literals changes an impossible existential condition
into a satisfiable parameter condition. The dense-order proof inherits this
issue. Also, an atomic formula on a larger variable list need not itself be a
complete pattern; it must be expressed as a disjunction of such patterns.

**Repair and corpus disposition:** discard inconsistent full patterns before
projecting, or eliminate equality by substitution and order bounds by retaining
all parameter conditions and every lower/upper comparison.
[Quantifier elimination](entries/quantifier-elimination/entry.html#equality-elimination)
and its dense-order argument use these repairs; the formal finite-pattern proof
ranges only over patterns realized by tuples. The motivational claim before
Theorem 6.3.4 that there are only three quantifier-free possibilities also omits
Boolean combinations; same-pattern tuples with different between-point behavior
supply the correct non-elimination argument. Later algebraic applications are
outside the adopted scope.
